subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Columbia Disaster: Foam That Killed
description: One-minute skill: The Columbia Disaster: Foam That Killed.

hook.text: On February 1, 2003, Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during re-entry. All seven astronauts were lost.

buildup.text: During launch, a piece of insulating foam broke off the external tank and struck the orbiter's left wing.

discovery.text: The foam punched a hole in the reinforced carbon-carbon heat shield. During re-entry, superheated plasma entered the wing.

twist.text: Engineers requested satellite imagery to inspect damage in orbit. Management denied it, calling the foam a minor issue.

climax.text: NASA reformed its safety culture again. Future missions carried repair kits and could shelter at the International Space Station.

punchline.text: A piece of foam. A hole in the wing. A culture that dismissed warnings.

quiz.question: What did engineers request after the foam strike that management denied?
options: An emergency spacewalk to inspect the wing surface in orbit
Satellite imagery to assess the damage to the heat shield
An early return to Earth before further damage could occur
